subject: Follow-up: hosting vs reserved GPU — recommended path and next steps
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@catalyst-ai.com>, ops@catalyst-ai.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: hosting vs reserved GPU — recommended path and next steps

Hi Maria / Catalyst ops team,

Thanks again for the call earlier — good to have clarity on the traffic shape and latency constraints. Quick recap and my recommended path so we can align on next steps:  

Recap of requirements (what I heard)
- Target p95 latency: ~50 ms for single-turn text generation (low-batched, user-interactive).
- Expected sustained throughput: 150–220 req/s during peak windows; occasional bursts to ~350 req/s for short bursts (a few minutes).
- Model family: ~13B open model (you mentioned fine-tuning on a domain corpus later).
- Data residency: US primary, no immediate need for on-prem.
- Compliance: standard enterprise controls; SOC2 evidence may be requested during procurement.

Initial recommendation (summary)
- Short term: Hosted API trial (2 weeks) configured with burst credits + prefix caching to validate correctness and latency in prod-like traffic. Good for fast time-to-value and integration testing.
- Medium term: Reserved (dedicated) GPU pool for predictable SLOs and throughput — we recommend H100-backed dedicated capacity if you need sustained 200+ req/s with p95 < 60 ms at production traffic.
- Long term: Private VPC/on‑prem can be considered if/when strict data residency or audit controls mandate it.

Why reserved capacity for your case
- Sustained throughput: continuous batching and KV cache on dedicated pools yields lower per-token cost and steadier latency at high sustained QPS.
- Latency SLOs: we can tune kernel selection and instance sizing on a dedicated pool to hit 50 ms p95 more reliably than shared-hosted in many scenarios.

Proposed next steps
1) Please confirm whether latency (p95) is the primary constraint vs cost/time-to-market.
2) If latency is critical, we propose scheduling a technical deep-dive with our SEs (Karthik) to review traffic patterns and run a small latency-focused bench. (30–45 min)
3) We can spin a 2-week hosted trial with 100k token credit and burst allowance while we scope a 4–6 week dedicated PoC.
4) Procurement: I attached a short SLA brief and a draft capacity quote for your review. Let me know your procurement timeline and any PO process details.

Attachments: [attachment: redwood-sla-brief.pdf], [attachment: capacity-quote-8721.xlsx]

If that plan works, I can coordinate times for the SE deep-dive — I'm proposing Wednesday or Thursday this week.

Cheers,
Rafael
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192
From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@catalyst-ai.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@catalyst-ai.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 18:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: hosting vs reserved GPU — recommended path and next steps

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for the clear summary — that aligns with what we discussed. A couple clarifications from our side:  
- Latency is indeed the most important metric for our user-facing flows. We need to target ~50 ms p95 or better.
- Sustained ~200 req/s is the realistic steady-state peak; bursts to ~350 for a few minutes are expected during launches/promos.
- We don’t have strict on-prem or data residency requirements today, but we will need SOC2 artifacts during the procurement window.

Questions:
1) What’s the typical lead time to provision reserved capacity (H100 pool)?
2) Can you provide a ballpark monthly cost for the dedicated setup versus hosted (we understand hosted is variable but we need a working estimate)?
3) We’d like to try the hosted trial to validate correctness and then run the dedicated PoC if results look good. How quickly can the trial start?

We’re targeting a decision within the next month. If you could get the SE deep-dive scheduled this week that’d help.

Thanks —
Maria Gomez
CTO, Catalyst AI
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: Catalyst AI — pricing/PoC plan

Karthik / Marissa — internal note before I reply to Maria:  

Plan I want to propose to the customer:
- Start hosted trial within 48 hours of signature (2-week window) with 100k token credit + transient burst allowance to simulate their 350 req/s bursts.
- Parallel: scoped dedicated PoC (H100 nodes) for 4–6 weeks to validate sustained 200 req/s at p95 < 60ms. SE scope: kernel tuning, batching config, KV cache priming.
- Ask for a 15% strategic PoC discount on the first 3 months of reserved commitment to make the economics attractive. (Need pricing approval.)
- Prepare SOC2 pack and SLA brief to attach to procurement packet.

Open asks for you both:
- Karthik: can you confirm SE availability for a deep-dive Wed or Thu and estimate how many H100 cards we’d propose for a 200 req/s steady target (ballpark)? Also please prepare a short checklist for the PoC (what metrics/logs we need).
- Marissa: can you review the attached draft quote and confirm a PoC discount we can offer without manager sign-off? If manager sign-off needed, I’ll escalate.

I’ll send Maria a reply with the proposed timeline and attach the SLA/quote.

Rafael
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@catalyst-ai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: hosting vs reserved GPU — recommended path and next steps

Hi Maria —

Appreciate the quick confirmation. Short answers to your questions and proposed timeline:  

1) Lead time for reserved capacity: provisioning for an H100-backed dedicated pool and initial sizing typically takes 4–6 weeks (including image/config, kernel tuning, and smoke tests). We can accelerate to ~3 weeks if we push an exec prioritization, but that’s the optimistic case.

2) Ballpark costs (monthly, US region) — very rough estimates to help internal budgeting:  
- Hosted API (variable): ~$8k–$20k / month for your expected usage band (depends on token volume and caching).
- Reserved / Dedicated (H100 pool): starting from ~$65k/month for a minimal cluster sized to sustain 200 req/s at low-latency; scales up with headroom.
(We’ll send a firm quote — draft attached.)

3) Hosted trial start: we can provision the 2-week hosted trial within 48 hours; I’ve attached the SLA brief and the draft capacity quote for Catalyst (see attachments).

Proposed next steps (concrete)
- SE deep-dive (30–45 min): Wed 11:00 AM PT or Thu 2:00 PM PT — please confirm which works. Karthik will run latency/tuning checklist.
- I’ll enable the hosted trial once you confirm and sign the short trial agreement (we can use e-sign).
- Parallel: we’ll scope dedicated PoC and share a firm quote + expected provisioning timeline.

Attachments: [attachment: redwood-sla-brief.pdf], [attachment: capacity-quote-8721.xlsx]

If that looks right, confirm the SE slot and I’ll lock it in.

Best,
